source.title: Data-Centric Interpretability for LLM-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: J. Yan; Michael Yu; Yu-Qing Sun; Alexandra Duffy; Tyler Marques; Matthew Lyle Olson

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether SAE-derived features characterize interpretable behaviors in LLM-generated data, an indirect test of V4. It does not test superposition geometry or capacity pressure.
record.gate_note: The study applies a pretrained SAE to Diplomacy trajectories and evaluates feature-derived hypotheses. Its results on feature interpretation and validation bear indirectly on V4. It does not measure overlap, feature directions, dimensional capacity, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical. Prompt templates in the paper instruct task-specific LLMs; none address an AI reading or reviewing this paper.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pretrained Gemma Scope 2 SAE as a tagging tool on Qwen3 Diplomacy text. It reports only its own pipeline's performance: hypothesis significance with LLM judges, expert ratings, user-study uplift, and prompt intervention. It never measures whether the model's representations are superposed, whether the SAE recovers the model's features (reconstruction, coverage, spread across neurons), or whether features are canonical or 1-D. The SAE results describe properties of the text dataset and the usefulness of the method, not evidence that LLMs contain recoverable sparse features, so this is T4 rather than a test of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SAE Meta-Autointerp and LLM summarization give complementary views of RL training behavior, and that 90% of SAE Meta-Features are significant under automated validation. They also find that not all interpretable features are useful: some seemingly helpful SAE features hurt human performance, while a subset predicts training dynamics. Adding discovered hypotheses to an untrained agent's prompt raised its score by 14.2%.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a pretrained Gemma Scope 2 SAE on LLM-generated Diplomacy trajectories for data-centric feature discovery and hypothesis validation; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that results vary with feature aggregation and correlation method, model layer and size, and data source; combining SAEs and data sources gives a 94% significance rate versus the reported 90% canonical run.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual SAE features, even when correctly explained by autointerp, were often not actionable alone. Only 45% (9/20) of their hypotheses improved LLM-judge early/late classification, versus 90% for grouped Meta-Features. Human ratings were also lower (helpfulness 0.63 vs 0.85).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single SAE features are often too fine-grained to be useful explanatory units for downstream tasks; grouping features improves their usefulness.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one environment and a small number of training runs. The paper notes that feature-outcome correlations are largely not causal, and its intervention combines multiple hypotheses rather than testing each separately. Human ratings use three experts; several results are aggregate measures of hypothesis usefulness rather than direct tests of SAE representation quality.
record.rows_left_out: Individual hypothesis results in Table 4 and user-study predictive-accuracy results were omitted because they assess downstream usefulness of particular behavior hypotheses rather than feature recovery itself. Other exploratory feature and training-run results were omitted for the same reason.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition, or feature geometry.
No capacity competition or neuron-level polysemanticity.
No measure of features spread across neurons, SAE reconstruction or recovery of model features. The SAE is used only as a text-tagging tool.
No test of completeness, stability across SAEs, or canonicity of SAE features.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The SAE is applied to Qwen3-generated text via Gemma 3 activations, a data-centric use. The record's subject (the Gemma SAE) does not correspond to a model whose representations are tested for superposition. The reader's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed because no row measures what V4 names.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, overcomplete sparse features, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry are tested.
No capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or neuron polysemanticity is tested.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are investigated.

The study provides indirect evidence from SAE-derived features in one data-centric setting. It does not measure features spread across neurons, directly validate SAE reconstruction against ground truth, or establish feature coverage across models or tasks.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features is made.

rows.subject: gemma-scope-2-27b-it-resid post: layer 31 width 262k l0 medium
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE feature activations against training-step trends and compared them with normalized keyword frequencies and feature-label/document embedding similarity.

conditions.value: keyword counts and embedding cosine similarity

rows.measure: Association of activation values with keyword frequencies and cosine similarity across training
rows.value: The authors report a strong correlation; no coefficient is stated.
rows.note: This is indirect evidence that SAE features track identifiable textual patterns in this dataset, not a test of completeness or representation geometry.
rows.check: Keyword and embedding validation of feature labels against training-step trends checks the study's own feature descriptions. No coefficient is given, and it does not measure SAE recovery of model features.

rows.subject: gemma-scope-2-27b-it-resid post: layer 31 width 262k l0 medium
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated whether SAE Meta-Feature hypotheses improved LLM-judge early-versus-late training classification.

conditions.value: Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT-5 Mini, and Grok 4.1 Fast pooled

rows.measure: Fraction of SAE Meta-Feature hypotheses deemed significant for predictive usefulness
rows.baseline: Accuracy without the hypothesis; exact aggregate baseline not stated
rows.uncertainty: A hypothesis was significant when accuracy improved and p < 0.05 by McNemar’s test.
rows.note: This evaluates downstream usefulness of aggregated SAE-feature hypotheses, not whether SAE features are canonical model units.
rows.check: The study's own method (Meta-Autointerp) is compared with other hypothesis sources on a downstream classification task. This is method performance, not a measure of superposition or feature recovery.

rows.subject: gemma-scope-2-27b-it-resid post: layer 31 width 262k l0 medium
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated whether individual SAE-feature hypotheses improved LLM-judge early-versus-late training classification.

conditions.value: Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT-5 Mini, and Grok 4.1 Fast pooled

rows.measure: Fraction of individual SAE-feature hypotheses deemed significant for predictive usefulness
rows.baseline: Accuracy without the hypothesis; exact aggregate baseline not stated
rows.uncertainty: A hypothesis was significant when accuracy improved and p < 0.05 by McNemar’s test.
rows.note: Fewer than half of the sampled individual SAE hypotheses met the stated significance criterion.
rows.check: Downstream predictive usefulness of individual SAE-feature hypotheses, used as a comparator to the study's own method. It does not bear on V4. The 'partial' state is not meaningful for any version.

rows.subject: gemma-scope-2-27b-it-resid post: layer 31 width 262k l0 medium
rows.operation_detail: Had three Diplomacy experts rate SAE Meta-Feature hypotheses.
rows.note: These ratings concern grouped SAE-derived hypotheses, not feature completeness or stability.
rows.check: Expert ratings of the study's own Meta-Feature hypotheses measure method output quality, not model representation.

rows.subject: gemma-scope-2-27b-it-resid post: layer 31 width 262k l0 medium
rows.operation_detail: Had three Diplomacy experts rate individual SAE-feature hypotheses.
rows.note: The authors report higher ratings for Meta-Features than for individual SAE features.
rows.check: Expert ratings of individual SAE-feature hypotheses compare against the study's own method. They do not measure the claim.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 SAEs across model sizes and layers, and gemma-scope-2-27b-it-resid post on additional data sources
rows.operation_detail: Combined features from multiple SAEs and data sources in one Meta-Autointerp run and assessed hypothesis significance.

conditions.value: Middle layers across model sizes; multiple layers of the 27B model
Raw trajectories and two summarized-trajectory variants

rows.baseline: 90% (26/29) for the single canonical SAE and data source
rows.note: The authors describe the increase over the canonical run as marginal and state that significance rates did not differ greatly across models, layers, and data sources.
rows.check: Significance rate of the pipeline across SAEs and data sources is an ablation of the study's method. The baseline (90%) is the study's own canonical run.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-derived behavioral features in the studied Diplomacy trajectory setting
reader_labels.reason: Feature activations were reported to correlate strongly with keyword and embedding checks, and aggregated SAE hypotheses received expert ratings and frequently met the predictive-significance criterion (R1, R2, R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Only 45% met the predictive-significance criterion, and their mean expert helpfulness and interpretability ratings were lower than those of Meta-Features (R3, R5).
